title: MotionKB body-part action fact (motionkb/v4)
description: Canonical contract for one agent/animation_knowledge_base/actions/<key>.json (v4). 9 channels = 8 anatomical + 1 root (kinematic-only). A record answers exactly two questions: what does this action LOOK like (action_description) and how does each body part MOVE (channels.*.motion_description + the kinematic block). Nothing else. v4 breaks v3 by DELETING every field that encoded a composition decision -- display_name, tags, mask_coverage, ik_goals, the whole composability block, and the per-channel role/motion_type/contact/constraint/target -- and by renaming overall_intent to action_description. Those decisions are not properties of a clip: whether an arm is free to be overridden, what a hand touches, which effector an IK goal pins and where, and who owns a channel in a blend all depend on the task being performed and the scene it is performed in, neither of which the knowledge base can see. They are made at runtime by the agent, which has both. What stays here is what a clip is true about on its own: measured kinematics (program-generated from the frozen raw/ pose dumps, never fabricated -- ADR 0002) and descriptions of the movement (VLM-proposed from rendered frames + those kinematics -- ADR 0008). Each channel carries two orthogonal kinematic facts: VARIATION -- state_label/motion_magnitude/raw_measurement, how much it moves -- and its MEAN POSE -- mean_pose on the anatomical channels, mean_body_height + mean_body_tilt_deg on the root -- stored as the vector it is and compared with nothing (ADR 0021). Cross-field invariants JSON Schema cannot express (every channel key is a known channel in engine_mask_map.json; an accepted record carries its descriptions) are enforced by validate_motionkb.py. action_id/action_description/motion_description are nullable because a record whose KINEMATIC half is complete and whose descriptions have not been proposed yet is a real state of the pipeline; validate_motionkb.py requires them the moment status is anything other than 'candidate' (ADR 0014).

action_description.description: One sentence saying what the whole action looks like. Was called overall_intent through v3; the rename is the point of v4 -- a record describes an appearance, it does not declare an intent, and an intent is what the runtime agent brings to it.

motion_description.description: One short plain-language sentence of what this body part does in this clip. The only semantic field a channel carries in v4. It says how the part MOVES -- not what it is for, not what it may be overridden by, not what it touches, all of which are readings the task and the scene supply.

mean_body_height.description: Mean HumanPose.bodyPosition.y over the clip, in normalised humanoid units (NOT metres, and not the sampled body's scale). Crouching and lying read low. Stored as the clip's own mean, not as an offset from a reference carriage.

mean_body_tilt_deg.description: Mean angle, in degrees, between bodyRotation's up axis and world up. Lying reads ~90. No anatomical muscle shows this: a corpse pose lies with straight legs and a straight spine, muscle-identical to standing at rest. Mean XZ and mean heading are deliberately absent -- both are properties of where the clip was authored, and how far the body travels is already the root's variation signal.

meanPose.description: The per-frame mean of each of this channel's Unity Humanoid muscle degrees of freedom, in the normalised muscle space the variation signal already uses ([-1, 1] over each DOF's HumanTrait range; 0 is that range's centre, which is a coordinate origin and not a rest pose). Keys are the engine's own muscle DOF names and are WRITTEN in ascending Unity muscle index within the channel, so two records list a channel's degrees of freedom in the same order and a diff between them lines up. This is a fact, not a classification: nothing here is reduced to a scalar, compared with a reference pose, or thresholded. It is what distinguishes an arm raised and held from an arm hanging still, which read identically on variation (ADR 0021).
